Not the original taste
Nov 2019
They tried so hard to create the flavor of Hai Phong food but I can tell that they didn't successful on doing that although they have many customers. I had lunch there sometimes and I know the original flavor so I'm sure that it was not original taste of Hai Phong food. From the beginning, they brought out chilly sauce which they named " Chiu Truong" but actually it was named "Chi chuong". Recently, I saw they untagged the spices and which was quite ok. I tried Banh da cua An Bien. The taste was quite ok. It should be some trace of crabs there but there was nothing show that the broth was made from crabs. Banh Da stuck together, I'm sure they didn't put the broth in quick enough to prevent it from sticking together. They used the fat part of meat in a wrong way. Cut it small and let it stay white like some kind of vegetables but the taste was awful, they should try to fry it until it turns into dark yellow. For drink, I tried Daisy tea which contained no tea at all. The right way to make it is to add some green tea and boil together with daisy. The drink tasted like water and with smell of daisy. It needed more strong taste and more sugar or syrup with a kumquat. Staff was nice and friendly

Great meal!
Nov 2017 • Family
I stumbled upon An Bien walking around and decided to try it. I did not regret taking a chance! I ordered the grilled mackerel and the sea crab spring roll. I enjoyed the spring roll a lot but the mackerel is so sumptuous! The combination of the fish with the carrots and pineapple with the basil in the wrap just made the meal so yummy. I could go on and on but you'd just have to try it. It didn't hurt that the owner was very attentive and answered a lot of questions I had regarding Hanoi, things to see, tours, other food, coffee etc.
